paper_metadata.title: A MODULAR ENGINE FOR QUANTUM MONTE CARLO INTEGRATION

summary: The paper presents Quantinuum’s Quantum Monte Carlo Integration (QMCI) engine implementing Fourier‑based QMCI with QPE‑free amplitude estimation variants (LCU QAE, MLQAE, IQAE). Simulator benchmarks show quadratic RMSE scaling (O(q⁻¹) vs classical O(q⁻¹/²)) and resource estimates for financial derivatives requiring roughly 117–439 qubits and up to 7.76×10⁷ gates (or 7.54×10⁸ T gates fault‑tolerant), but all evaluations are performed via simulation and resource modeling.

experiments.description: Quantum Monte Carlo integration benchmarks for pricing/evaluating financial instruments using a 6-qubit Gaussian or lognormal distribution loader and QPE-free amplitude estimation (MLQAE/LCU QAE/IQAE/PAM) on simulator; includes convergence and robustness studies.

algorithm.variant: QMCI with Fourier-series decomposition; QPE-free QAE variants (LCU QAE, MLQAE, IQAE, prepare-and-measure)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed number of uses q / target RMSE; for IQAE, stopping when confidence interval width <= 2ϵ

hyperparameters.q: number of uses of circuit A / P
hyperparameters.m: Fourier harmonic index (EIS uses m in {0,1,2,4,8,16,...})
hyperparameters.pmax_fail: upper bound on LCU failure probability
hyperparameters.nshots: 66 for m=0; 44 for m>0 in robustness benchmarks
hyperparameters.target_rmse: varies by benchmark; e.g. 1.04e-2 for value payoff in finance benchmarks
hyperparameters.sigma: 0.1 for exponential expectation benchmark; 0.12 for Gaussian benchmark in Fig. 32
hyperparameters.x_star: 0 for conditional expectation / conditional exponential expectation benchmarks

algorithm.parameter_initialization: LCU categories choose initial angles within allowed ranges; amplitude benchmarks vary θ to prepare target amplitudes

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: LCU beta constrained by 0 <= beta <= arcsin(sqrt(pmax_fail))

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Probability distribution loaded into qubit amplitudes; final qubit amplitude encodes expectation via controlled rotations and QAE
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[g(X)] for g in {x, conditional expectation, x^2, exp(x), conditional exp(x), Bernoulli qubit} using Fourier QMCI
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Indicator qubits from enhanced P-builder for conditional expectations; periodic piecewise extension of g(x) over support
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: additional ancilla for LCU state preparation; exact count not specified

problem_instance.description: Synthetic discrete approximations of Gaussian and lognormal random variables; benchmarked on 32-point and 64-point distributions and on financial payoff examples
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Continuous distributions discretized on uniform grids; support truncated to ±5σ; for finance benchmarks, return-space Brownian motion built by summing iid Gaussian increments
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10000 simulator repetitions per configuration for QAE robustness; bootstrap confidence intervals; resource estimates for benchmark instruments

quantum_resources.qubit_type: unspecified (algorithmic qubit counts; not logical error-corrected qubits)

error_correction.code_type: Clifford+T synthesis assumed for fault-tolerant resource mode

hardware.provider: not explicitly specified (simulations executed via pytket/state‑vector simulator)

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: LCU QAE statistical robustness; noise-aware QAE discussed but not used in the reported benchmark simulations

implementation_details.transpilation_target: {TK1, CNOT} for NISQ resource mode; Clifford+T for fault-tolerant mode
implementation_details.classical_solver: bootstrap confidence intervals; MMSE estimator; classical post-processing for QAE and resource estimation

transpilation_settings.basis_gates: TK1, CNOT; Clifford+T for FT mode

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Distribution discretization; PQC training for Gaussian/lognormal loaders; Fourier-series construction of periodic piecewise payoff functions
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: MMSE estimation; bootstrap CIs; resource counting; affine rescaling back to original support

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: QAE RMSE, bias, skewness, and kurtosis versus uses; distribution-loader training loss versus circuit depth

results.unit: shots (each m>0 in LCU benchmark protocol)

speedup_claims.conditions: for QMCI with QAE-based estimation; assuming the distribution is encoded as a quantum state and the Fourier-series decomposition is used
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper emphasizes that the advantage is in RMSE/sample complexity; practical usefulness depends on distribution loading and circuit resources.

speedup_claims.conditions: for the benchmark finance problems when target RMSE is around 1% of support range
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this is the crossover regime for quantum advantage in sample complexity, not a full end-to-end wall-clock advantage.

speedup_claims.factor: approximately 100 qubits and 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity may suffice for some simple finance QMCI calculations
speedup_claims.conditions: future hardware, low-volatility single-asset path-dependent benchmarks
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a speculative resource estimate, not an experimental demonstration.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: RMSE scales as O(q^-1) for QAE-based QMCI; resource mode gives qubit/gate scaling for benchmark problems
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical Monte Carlo RMSE scales as O(q^-1/2)
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: c_QAE values reported: LCU QAE 13.3 worst-case finite-use bound, 7.82 asymptotic; MLQAE 8.02; IQAE 14.4; PAM 0.5
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_classical: 1/2 in the bound RMSE <= range/(2 sqrt(q)) for classical MCI
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Not given as a single closed form; benchmark totals reported in tables
complexity_analysis.crossover_n: Table 6 reports crossover RMSE percentages of support: mean/conditional expectation 1.12% (LCU), 1.86% (MLQAE), 1.03% (IQAE); second moment 0.67%, 1.11%, 0.61%; exponential/conditional exponential 0.72%, 1.20%, 0.67%; Bernoulli 1.88%, 3.12%, 1.73%

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Quantum advantage in sample complexity predicted when RMSE ≈ 0.6–3.1% of support depending on estimator (Table 6), but no real‑hardware validation.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Benchmark circuits require 117–439 qubits and up to 7.76×10^7 gates (NISQ resource estimates) or up to 7.54×10^8 T gates for fault‑tolerant estimates (Tables 8–9).
limiting_factors: Large circuit depth and gate counts in realistic financial benchmarks.
State preparation complexity for probability distributions.
Need for large qubit counts (100–400+) even for simplified examples.
Reliance on simulators rather than real quantum hardware.

notes: The paper reports simulator-based numerical experiments for QAE robustness and resource estimates for finance benchmarks; no real QPU execution is described.
Distribution-loader resource tables (Tables 4 and 5) and finance benchmark resource tables (Tables 8 and 9) provide the qubit/gate counts used here.
The paper includes multiple QAE variants; they are grouped into one experiment because they evaluate the same QMCI framework with different QAE subroutines and problem settings.
The authors explicitly describe the advantage as theoretical and emphasize resource estimates rather than experimental demonstrations.
All quantitative experiments are performed on simulators and resource‑estimation tools.

experiments.description: Benchmark of parameterised quantum circuit (PQC) distribution loaders for Gaussian and lognormal distributions using hardware‑efficient and tensor‑network ansatz circuits.

algorithm.variant: PQC state preparation for probability distributions
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient ansatz and brickwall tensor‑network ansatz
algorithm.optimizer: classical minimization of L∞, L1, and L2 norms (final experiments use L2)

key_results: Gaussian distribution loader circuits achieve L∞ error ≈ 10⁻⁵–10⁻⁶ with ~50–142 gates and 20–46 CNOTs (Tables 4–5).
Tensor‑network training achieves extremely small divergence (≈10⁻¹⁴ KL divergence) but with larger circuit depth.
